environment: Linux, JDK 21, clean isolated checkout; record host, toolchain and clean source status
head: c5d4ca375396006460a72e97aa99d34337780580
requirements: Verify exact fork head and ancestry; capture commands, exit codes, fresh logs and JUnit XML with counts, failures and skips.

Run ./gradlew :solr:core:cleanTest :solr:core:test --tests org.apache.solr.update.SolrCmdDistributorTest with recorded seed, then repeat testStallKeepsErrorsFromOtherNodes under multiple seeds. Require bounded execution, actual retry, both expected errors, and commit and delete-by-query refusing the stalled flush. Run ./gradlew tidy and ./gradlew check -x test. A tracked formatting change invalidates proof; require committed successor and new gate.

Fail-before: in a disposable checkout at this head retain the test and revert only round-3 production changes to contributor production; confirm the ordering boundary assertion fails at runtime. Separately restore baseline production before PR 5330 while retaining the executable test and demonstrate lost-error regression or document accurately if a separate minimal test overlay is needed. Capture overlays, commands, logs and XML; compilation, setup, timeout and skip are not behavioral proof.

Review and test retries after a stall, multiple stalled clients, suppression, finish error retention, pending asynchronous work, and whether a late runner callback can change replication accounting after the stall. Add a bounded diagnostic as needed; if an actual safety concern is unresolved, do not mark clean. Record how queued work and shared-executor shutdown behave; the patch fences later DBQ/commit but does not cancel an active runner.
Do not change or push source from the gate. Any failures or fixes require a separate scoped implementation and a superseding exact-head gate. No public post.
verdict_policy: Pass only if named tests, root checks and meaningful fail-before legs succeed and no material correctness concern remains. Distinguish late-callback limitations from the protected ordered-operation boundary.
